messages:
maya: Quick thread — hit a race on staging where eviction applied after a lease revoke and caused read-after-write failures for a long-lived cursor. timeline + notes below.

liam: Can you paste minimal repro or logs?

maya: Logs snippet from staging: 
```
[2026-03-20T12:01:10Z] lease_revoke epoch=42 prefix=pfx/123
[2026-03-20T12:01:10Z] evict_decision epoch=41 prefix=pfx/123 chosen_by=node-7
[2026-03-20T12:01:10Z] cursor_resume read -> tombstone/error
```

maya: TL;DR: eviction worker can make a decision based on a stale epoch view. lease revoke increments epoch but that update isn't always observed by the evict worker before apply (we saw >200ms fanout tail during jitter). result: we evict a prefix we thought was still leased.

jordan: Ouch. Sounds like ordering between lease metadata fanout and eviction apply is weak. Did evict worker look up meta at apply time or rely on queued observed_epoch?

maya: Today: when we schedule an eviction we stash observed_epoch, but apply path is asynchronous and can read stale meta if fanout hasn't arrived. Sometimes worker doesn't re-read meta before applying because of perf-critical fastpath.

devon: Two fixes: 
1) synchronous metadata re-read at apply time (safe but adds sync rtt on every evict apply -> tail latency hit).
2) introduce an eviction fence token written by lease revoke; evict worker compares token/epoch before applying. cheaper reads but needs extra meta and fanout guarantee semantics.

liam: Option 1 kills throughput on hot prefixes. Option 2 adds metadata churn. Which is less bad?

maya: Proposed hybrid: keep fastpath but make it conservative: attach observed_epoch to queued eviction; at apply time attempt a cheap read of meta. If meta epoch > observed_epoch => skip/abandon. If read fails due to transient, push back to queue with exponential backoff (bounded). That avoids synchronous strong ordering but prevents obvious races. Pseudocode:
```
on_schedule_evict(prefix):
  item.observed_epoch = meta_cache.get_epoch(prefix)
  queue.push(item)

evict_worker_process(item):
  meta = meta_service.get(prefix)  // cheap local read with ~1us memcache if warm
  if meta.epoch > item.observed_epoch:
    metrics.inc("evict_skipped_epoch_mismatch")
    continue
  apply_evict(prefix)
```

jordan: Edge case: what if evict_worker reads meta before revoke write arrives (still stale) then apply -> still wrong. The difference is we compared observed_epoch taken at schedule vs meta at apply; if both stale we can still be unsafe. Need guarantee that revoke writes will bump meta. Only way to avoid is to ensure fanout happens-before eviction apply (strong ordering) or to use a revocation sentinel that blocks apply until observed.

devon: Right. Another variant: when lease_revoke happens, also push a high-priority "revoke fence" item into eviction queue for that prefix. Worker processes fence items before normal evicts for same prefix. That gives ordering via queue semantics, not synchronous RPC. It relies on queue ordering/priority and cross-node processing guarantees though.

liam: That could work if we can guarantee fence item arrives earlier than any in-flight evict for that prefix. But network reordering: fence write could be slower than an already in-flight evict. To be correct we'd need eviction apply to check meta epoch anyway. So fence alone is not sufficient.

maya: So we need both: fence + epoch-check at apply. Fence helps reduce races in the common case; epoch-check is safety net.

devon: Perf thoughts: epoch-check should be optimized: store epoch in a local strongly-consistent meta cache with fast invalidation on fanout. Lease_fanout should invalidate local shards' cache entries immediately when writing revoke. That minimizes remote reads.

jordan: Also, account for splits/merges: epoch semantics must be per key-range. When split happens, child ranges inherit epoch but need independent progression. Update RFC to include split semantics.

liam: Ops: add metric evict_skipped_epoch and evict_applied_after_revoke as counter; alert if applied_after_revoke > 0.1% of evictions in a window. Also add canary with chaos: delay lease fanout by X ms to reproduce.

maya: Proposed rollout plan: 
- implement fence+epoch-check with local meta-cache invalidation optimization 
- unit + chaos tests (inject fanout delays)
- canary flag: evict_epoch_check=true in 1 region at 50% traffic
- collect metrics and perf delta (p95 apply latency)

opsbot: deploy-bot: canary started region=us-east-1 flag=evict_epoch_check=true pct=50

jordan: SGTM. I'll draft RFC covering tradeoffs (throughput hit, added meta field, cache invalidation complexity, split/merge semantics). Include perf microbench: check 99th p99 apply latency + CPU.

devon: Also propose a small simulation harness: run a micro-sim that injects random fanout delays and asserts no read-after-write failures for N=1e6 ops. command: `go test ./evictsim -run TestLeaseEvictRace -tags=sim -count=1`

maya: I'll open RFC & link it here. Thanks all.

maya: RFC: https://go/repo/rfcs/evict-epoch-fence (placeholder)
